arc: Vic asks his daughter to marry in the morning and cannot tell her what time kick-off is; the six tickets cannot leave his phone and he cannot leave the wedding, so after nine weeks of typing Danny sends four words, "Leave it with me.", and Maya, who does not know what "it" is, leaves it with him. Danny takes Vic's flight, but the airline needs a surname and nobody has one: eleven years, and he is "Danny Football" in every phone; only his grandmother knows it. On the Saturday the phone flies and Vic does not: the flight changed its name for a fee, the tickets will not, the T-shirts are right for one day, and both typing indicators are Danny. Lee finds it cheaper: three flights and a bus, an hour longer than coming from Sydney, arriving before kick-off, depending on kick-off. On match day Jo, who never said she was coming, is at the gate; Sydney has been behind Maya since five; six tickets on one phone go in together, so they wait for Lee, and the time is finally confirmed by the kick-off itself, with the same two inside as last season. The season ends with the group having seen nineteen minutes and calling it the best one they have done: five pay that night, Vic has said Friday and is recorded as having attended his twelfth match from his daughter's wedding, Danny answers the chat's first question with "I'm in.", and the grandmother's last status is WENT.

why: Why this continuation: every film turns on one person doing exactly what that person does, so the finale needs no new jokes, only consequences. Vic, who buys tickets to matches he cannot go to, has bought six more and is recorded as attending from his daughter's wedding (ATTENDED 11 becomes 12). Jo, who never said yes, is at the gate; her "Should be fine." is said once more, one minute before it is not. Sydney, who answers at two in the morning, has been behind Maya since five and is still never seen. Lee compares until the route takes longer than Sydney's. Danny cannot finish a message but, like his grandmother, simply goes: he collects the phone, delivers it, and is inside with her for kick-off, the same two and the same shot as Episode 1. Maya lets go once ("I've left it with him") and gives the verdict fans really give. Each film is built on one thing a traveller recognises at once: the tickets are always on the phone of the one who cannot come; you know a man eleven years as "Danny Football"; the cheaper route; the organiser is paid on the way home, when the trip was good. Every thread is closed: wedding and phone (Ep 5, 6, 7), Danny's typing (sent in 5, ended in 7 by answering the chat's own title), name changes on flights (Short A, Ep 6), the Saturday T-shirts (right for one day, Ep 6), the 22 hours (Short B), "is it 7:45 or 8" (it was 7:45), the kick-off time (CONFIRMED is the season's last stamp, after two shorts end on TO BE CONFIRMED to set it up), OWE MAYA (6 to 1), "which Friday" (still Friday), two arrived (two inside again), "I just go" (WENT.). Limits: 445 narrator characters of 700 (counted); 7 new shots of 10, two extra stills (Danny's portrait, Vic in a suit), three shots held back for retakes; lengths 29.7, 21.4, 27.9, 20.9 and 34.8 seconds; no new kind of graphic. Biggest risk: the finale carries eight beats in 34.8 seconds, right at the ceiling; each is one glance, but if the real takes run long the first thing to cut is the "Paid." cascade's narrator line, never the stamp's silence or Maya's verdict. Other risks, stated plainly: Danny is inside at kick-off on a ticket nobody explains (deliberate, the same rule as his grandmother, but a literal viewer may count six tickets and ask); Vic in a suit and Danny's new face both depend on a redraw holding the likeness; Lee's unused "Again." stays unused, because here the kick-off never moves again: it is confirmed by happening, which I judged the stronger payoff. I changed no file and ran nothing except a character count.
